concepts.title: Why Earth Is a Unique Planet

questions.q: Why is earth called the blue planet?
questions.a: Seen from space, most of its surface (about three-fourths) is water, so it looks blue.

questions.q: Name two features that make earth special among planets.
questions.a: Liquid water and a life-supporting atmosphere (plus a safe distance from the sun).

questions.q: Why does earth have day and night?
questions.a: It spins on its axis once in about 24 hours, turning each side to face the sun.

concepts.title: The Planets of the Solar System

questions.q: Name the planets in order from the sun.
questions.a: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune.

questions.q: Which planets are called inner and outer planets?
questions.a: Inner: Mercury to Mars (rocky). Outer: Jupiter to Neptune (gas/ice giants).

questions.q: Why is Venus the hottest planet though Mercury is nearer the sun?
questions.a: Venus's thick carbon-dioxide blanket traps heat - a runaway greenhouse effect.

concepts.title: What Makes Earth Suitable for Life

questions.q: What makes earth suitable for life?
questions.a: Water, a breathable atmosphere with oxygen, and a mild temperature range maintained by its distance from the sun.

questions.q: How does the atmosphere protect life on earth?
questions.a: It holds oxygen, blocks harmful UV (ozone layer) and burns up most meteors.

questions.q: Why is earth's distance from the sun important for life?
questions.a: At this distance water stays liquid - nearer it would boil away, farther it would freeze.

questions.q: Name two natural cycles that sustain life on earth.
questions.a: The water cycle and the carbon (or nitrogen, oxygen) cycle.

questions.q: What is the ozone layer's role in sustaining life?
questions.a: It shields living things from the sun's harmful ultraviolet rays.

questions.q: How do oceans help keep earth livable?
questions.a: They hold water, make rain, absorb carbon dioxide and keep climate mild.

questions.q: Name two threats to life on earth today.
questions.a: Pollution of air and water, and climate change from greenhouse gases (also deforestation).

questions.q: How does cutting forests threaten life?
questions.a: It removes oxygen-makers and animal homes, raises CO2, and causes floods and soil loss.

questions.q: Suggest two actions to protect earth's life-support systems.
questions.a: Save energy and water, plant trees, recycle waste, and cut the use of plastics and fossil fuels.
